With a controller, use Rearrange this tab. releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7.2
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7.2 ## New - **ZeroFG frame generation:** (experimental) adds frames between the ones a game draws, x2, x3 or x4, up to your display's refresh rate. It's in Settings > Performance and in the in-game menu. Switch it on before starting a game, switched on during one, it starts after Apply & Restart. By @hy300leosquizz-ctrl (#331).

releases.name: ARMSX3 for iOS 0.0.4 beta
releases.body:
## Graphics and memory

**Faster frame submission.** MoltenVK now turns each frame into Metal work on its own thread instead of on the graphics thread, so the graphics thread spends almost no time submitting a frame. Framebuffers are now freed only after the GPU has finished with them, which this needed. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Freed textures give their memory back.** Large texture allocations now get memory of their own, which goes back to iOS when the texture is freed. Before, one texture still in use kept a whole 64 MB block, and One Piece held 2.3 GB of blocks for 643 MB of textures. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Upload buffer space comes back sooner.** The texture upload buffer gives back finished space after every full GPU wait, where it held it until the next frame and swapped in a new buffer instead.

**No stall on the first new shader.** The shader compiler's one-time setup now happens at boot. It used to land in gameplay, on the first shader a game hadn't shown before. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Black Ops II weapon.** The weapon in your hands no longer draws with its triangles over each other.

releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7.1
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7.1 ## Games - **Uncharted 2: Among Thieves, Super Street Fighter IV, Journey, and other games:** fixed the stop with "Failed to compile fragment shader" at the default Shader Precision (Low). - **Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction:** fixed the freeze on Cobalia (thanks Seeslo for testing). -**Uncharted 3: Drake’s Deception** gets The Last of Us fix for freezes during play, since both games run the same job system, prevents freezes in UC3. ## Save states - **Save states from 1.7 and earlier don't load in 1.7.1,** because RPCS3's font module update changed the save state format. In-game saves are not affected.

releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7 ## Highlights - **New SPU code compiles in the background.** Games keep running while it compiles, so new areas load without pausing. Games that need the old pause keep it. - **Compiled SPU code now carries over between updates,** including game updates, so first boots after them are quick. Each game compiles once more on its first boot after this update. ## The Last of Us - **Fixed the freeze during play.** The game hands its work to background jobs and waits for them, and on phones a job list could stop with work still in it, freezing the game anywhere from minutes to hours in. ARMSX3 now keeps those jobs moving.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.9
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.9 gives the Commander X16's network card Zimodem's command-mode connections, so programs that open several connections at once, like Veranda's Gemini, Gopher, FTP and chat programs, now connect.

## What's new

- **Veranda's network programs connect.** The X16's network card now handles the Zimodem commands that [Veranda](https://github.com/veranda-x16/veranda) uses to keep several connections open at once. Its Gemini browser, Gopher client, FTP and chat programs can reach the internet from the emulator.
- **Secure connections.** Programs can now open encrypted (TLS) connections through the X16's network card, which Gemini and HTTPS need. As on the real card, the card does the encryption itself and doesn't check the server's certificate.

## Downloads

| macOS, Apple Silicon   | `_aarch64.dmg`              |
| macOS, Intel           | `_x64.dmg`                  |

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.8
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.8 brings the Apple II to phones and tablets, turns the touch screen into the Commander X16's mouse and the NES Zapper, and fixes the picture being cut off on phones with a gesture bar.

## What's new

- **The Apple II on a phone or tablet.** Hold it upright for a keyboard: Android's own, with rows of Esc, Tab, Ctrl, the arrows and Delete above it, plus Open Apple and Closed Apple, which stay down while you touch them. Reset only presses once you've held it for half a second, so a stray tap won't reset the machine. Turn it sideways for a joystick: an analog stick that moves as far as you push it, and buttons 0 and 1. Move it, resize it or hide it from the pause menu, as with the other pads.
- **The touch screen is the X16's mouse.** Drag a finger on the picture to move the pointer, tap to click, tap with two fingers to right-click, and tap then hold to drag. It works in the app and in the browser, so mouse programs like the Veranda desktop work on a phone.
- **Tap to shoot with the Zapper.** In Zapper games like Duck Hunt, tap the picture where you want to shoot.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.7
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.7 brings the Commander X16 to phones and tablets, with a keyboard in portrait and a SNES pad in landscape, gives the X16 all its function keys and proper SNES controllers everywhere, and tidies up Android.

## What's new

- **The X16 on a phone or tablet.** Hold it upright for a keyboard: Android's own, with autocorrect and suggestions off, and rows of Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, the arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down and Delete/Insert above it. Ctrl and Alt are sticky, so Ctrl then C sends Ctrl+C; tap twice to hold them. Fn brings up F1 to F12. Turn it sideways for a SNES pad.
- **Hide controls.** The pause menu on a touch screen can hide the on-screen controls for the rest of the game, and show them again.
- **The X16's F-keys are its own.** On the X16, and on the other computers that use the whole keyboard (Skink and BASIC), F1 to F12 go to the machine, so programs like busterm get them all. Open Bus's own keys move behind Ctrl+Shift: Ctrl+Shift+F1 opens the menu, Ctrl+Shift+F2 saves a state, and so on.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.6
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.6 lets you install the web version as an app that opens without the internet, and fixes a way to get stuck in a game on Android phones.

## What's new

- **Install the web version as an app.** At https://obus.tuxprint.com/, Chrome and Edge offer to install Open Bus with its own window and icon, and Settings → Library has an Install button where your browser supports it. On iPhone, use Share → Add to Home Screen.
- **The web version works offline.** Once it's been opened, it opens again with no internet connection. It still picks up updates whenever you're online.
- **Your games stay put in the browser.** When you first add a game, the page asks the browser not to clear your games when it runs low on space.

## Fixed

- **Stuck in the emulator's menu on an Android phone.** Pressing Select and Start together on the on-screen controls opened a menu the on-screen buttons couldn't work, so the only way out was to quit the game. On-screen Select and Start now go to the game. A gamepad's Select and Start still open the menu, and Back still pauses.

## Downloads

| System                 | File                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------- |

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.5
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.5 makes the Android app work on phones and tablets, with on-screen controls for NES games, and keeps the Commander X16's clock on time.

## What's new

- **On-screen controls for NES games** on a phone or tablet with no gamepad: a D-pad, A and B, Select and Start. They hide when a gamepad connects and come back when it disconnects.
- **Move controls.** Drag each piece where you want it, make them bigger or smaller, turn the vibration off, or put B higher than A. Your layout is kept.
- **A pause menu for touch screens.** Back opens it: Resume, Save state, Load state, Reset, Move controls and Quit. Before this, there was no way out of a game on a phone without a gamepad.
- **The library on phones** stays clear of the status bar, navigation bar, camera cutout and on-screen keyboard. Games are always fullscreen.
- **The sidebar with a gamepad.** On a phone, opening the sidebar moves the gamepad's selection into it.

## Fixed

- **A TV remote's OK** stopped choosing in the menus if you bound A to something else, and didn't work in the X16's menu at all. It now always works in the menus, whatever the controls are set to.

New audio, rendering, and Android startup fixes are here. Huge thanks to
[Andrew Nakas](https://github.com/andrewnakas) and contributors for the underlying
work, and [AlanConstantino](https://github.com/AlanConstantino) for integrating
it and testing on Retroid Pocket 6 in [PR #123](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/pull/123).
Alex McHugh's Skate3Recomp and ReXGlue/Xenia remain the foundation of this port.

## Download

Most players want **Skate3-Mobile-Android.apk**. Install over your existing
main app. Do not uninstall first. Android will ask you to approve the update.
Your extracted game files stay in place.

[Download the main APK](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/releases/download/v2.1.0/Skate3-Mobile-Android.apk)
or [get the separate QA Build](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/releases/download/v2.1.0-qa1/Skate3-Mobile-QA.apk).
The debug APK is for users of the separate developer app.

Older QA and developer builds used the main app's update address. Install the
matching v2.1 APK once, without uninstalling. From this version onward, each
app receives updates for its own package only.

## What changed

releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 6

This QA build targets an intermittent early-boot hang reported on the Retroid Pocket 5.

The failed QA 5 diagnostic showed a live audio thread but no first presentation, native pipeline creation, scene target, or crash. The guest render thread stopped immediately after its first offscreen 2D captures.

QA 6 tightens the boot capture boundary:

- Only the four verified 2D vertex layouts and three supported primitive types are accepted.
- Individual and per-frame 2D payloads have conservative size limits.
- Invalid transient draw state is rejected before reading guest memory.
- The first twelve guest frames now log capture begin and completion markers.

Install QA 6 over the previous QA app, keep the System Driver selected, fully close the app between attempts, and test at least five launches. Attach diagnostics from any failed launch.

The stable app and stable update channel are unchanged. The APK includes no game data.

releases.name: Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5
releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5

This is an opt-in diagnostic build that installs over earlier **Skate 3 QA** builds and preserves QA app data.

## RP5 intermittent black-screen fix

QA 4 proved that the Retroid Pocket 5 can render the Quality profile's 1280x720 scene target, but testers reported that startup only succeeded roughly half the time.

The QA 4 profile copied Performance's visible feature settings, but one internal pipeline gate still used the profile number. Quality therefore compiled optional outline, spline, and shadow shader families even though those features were disabled. Cold and partially warmed shader caches could take different startup paths.

QA 5 fixes the mismatch:

- The 1280x720 Quality target remains enabled.
- The pipeline builder now follows the active lean-scene flag instead of assuming every Quality profile needs the full optional PSO set.
- Renderer installation applies the same defensive lean-feature guard.
- The startup log must report `lean Android set` for this QA Quality profile.
- Stable v2.0.17 and its update channel remain unchanged.

## RP5 test

1. Install QA 5 directly over QA 4.
2. Keep the System Driver selected.

# 0.60.1 is out

There was a bug in the AppImage Updater Code. To fix this i have to revert to the old AppImage build and wait several weeks to ensure a smooth update process.

# 0.60.0 is out 🎉

This release is special for me. I build emuze with web technologies because that’s where I have the most experience, and I’m really proud of what I’ve achieved over the years. I’ve always wanted to help out in this wonderful emulation community, but aside from testing, I couldn’t do much to help with the emulators I love because I struggled with C++ code, which most emulators are written in. But sometimes you feel forced to try and try again. Since v0.59.0, I’ve successfully added a [change to RMG](https://github.com/Rosalie241/RMG/pull/518) to use the SDL GUID to identify a gamepad more reliably, and I forked Mednafen with [mednafen-sdl3](https://github.com/bmsuseluda/mednafen-sdl3) to greatly expand gamepad support. Those changes are just baby steps in the grand scheme of things, but they felt great, and I hope I can build on them in the future.

# 0.59.2 is out 🎉

This release is mostly preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0.
Besides this fuse2 is not necessary anymore and Metainfos for AppImage Managers e.g. AM are included.

Please let me know what you think of it in the [emuze discord](https://discord.gg/tCzK7kc6Y4).

## 💥 Features
- added AppImage Metainfos
- AppImage works without fuse2
- Preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0

# 0.59.0 is out 🎉

As you might now i love the simplicity of console gaming. You start the game and it just works. With emulation more often then not you have to provide more then just the game. You need things like a BIOS file, firmware or key files. I wanted to assist with this for a long time. With this release you can choose a folder where you can put your BIOS files and emuze will pick them up and configure the Emulators. Of course emuze will tell you if a required file is missing. On top of this emuze comes bundled with open source BIOS implementations for PlayStation, Game Boy Advance and NEO GEO. Of course you can use official BIOS files instead if you need by putting them in the BIOS folder. Sadly i was not able to achieve the same result for more complicated systems like PlayStation 3, WiiU and Switch. These systems require a installation of a firmware. I will try to tackle these in a future release.

Besides this i bundled and pre configured ScummVM and DOSBox Pure Unleashed.
Therefore the day is finally here: All 35 supported systems are pre configured and bundled now 🥳

# 0.58.0 is out 🎉

As one of the few nerdy kids in a small sleepy town in a country where arcade gaming was classified as gambling i could see lightgun games in magazines only. I had an NES and Captain N with his Zapper was sooo awesome to me. But when the time came that i could buy one with my own money the rise of flat panels began and with it the death of CRT TVs and Lightguns altogether. It was just a thing of the past, sadly.
But surprisingly the genre came back with the Wii and PS3 and there Pointer devices. Some years later camera based Lightguns came to the market and finally Lightgun gaming with the same and even higher precision is possible on flat panels.

## Endemic life is visible

Small creatures in the field (Stinkmink, Clothfly and the rest of the endemic life) were invisible in the port: you could still pick them up and get their buffs, but nothing was drawn. The game decides whether to draw them from a visibility test it runs on the GPU and then reads back on the CPU; the port never copied that result back, so the game always read "not visible". Now it does. Only that small result is copied, so the frame rate stays at a locked 30 fps.

- An empty file `sin_devolver_copias` in the game folder brings back the old behaviour.

Thanks to the player who reported it in issue #8.

Nothing else changes: shader caches are the same as in 1.6.0, so your existing caches keep working.

releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

The headline is that the hybrid JIT now translates **more than 80 % of the guest instruction
stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

| Windows x64 | `Model3-Vulkan.v0.9.9.8.for.Windows.zip` | Windows 10/11, Vulkan 1.3 |

**Windows only.** This release contains a single asset for Windows x64. Everything else is
v0.9.8.6 unchanged.

## Why the v0.9.8.6 Windows package refused to start on AMD graphics cards

On Windows, AMD's Vulkan driver reports **128 bytes** of push constants — the amount Vulkan itself
guarantees. Every driver this renderer had been developed against reports 256.

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

The headline is that the hybrid JIT now translates **more than 80 % of the guest instruction
stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. It is built from source and is not in the release archives. See [the libretro page](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro.md) and [the Mac guide](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro_macos.md).

Buildings falling by themselves, grabbing and eating, and a few smaller things from the same report.

# Lichii-Enhanced v1.0.0: first public release

Lichii-Enhanced is a fork of [Lichii](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii) focused on usability: easier setup, built-in upscaling, non-destructive modding and more reliable online play. This is the first public release.

> **Platform:** Windows 10/11 x64 only. Distributed as a `.zip` archive. Other platforms are not available yet.

## Highlights

### 🖼️ Built-in upscalers
Upscaling is now part of the renderer; no external injectors or wrappers are needed.

- New post-process stage at the end of the Vulkan frame (compute shaders), running after game rendering and before swapchain presentation
- Filters: Nearest, Bilinear, Bicubic, FSR 1.0 (EASU + RCAS), SGSR
- Configurable render scale and sharpness (RCAS strength)
- Per-game profiles stored in `config/custom/<title-id>.ini`
- Optional anti-aliasing pass before upscaling

- **Desempenho na Grande Ilha do Céu:**

releases.name: TOTKDroid 0.3.4 (beta): sem queda depois do menu e geração de quadros melhor
releases.body:
**Beta 0.3.4.** Acaba a **queda de fps depois de fechar o inventário** ([#53](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/53), [#24](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/24)) e melhora a **geração de quadros (LSFG)**: importar o `Lossless.dll`, funcionar em mais GPUs Mali e pedir à tela a taxa de atualização que os quadros gerados precisam.

> **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem junto.** Você precisa do seu próprio dump de *Tears of the Kingdom* com a atualização **1.4.3** aplicada (`exefs` e `romfs`, ou o `romfs` como um único `romfs.bin`).

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **Queda depois do menu ([#53](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/53), [#24](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/24)):**
  - A queda de 12-14 s depois de fechar o inventário, de escolher uma arma ou de salvar não era o clock da GPU, como eu tinha dito.
  - O app desligava o "sync lag" por ~10 s sempre que o jogo saía do mundo, para proteger os carregamentos. Só que ele não distinguia um menu de uma tela de carregamento, e nesses segundos a CPU ficava esperando a GPU.

releases.name: TOTKDroid 0.3.3 (beta): FSR 1 e FXAA mais leves
releases.body:
**Beta 0.3.3.** O **FSR 1** e o **FXAA** ficaram mais leves para a GPU, com a mesma imagem.

> **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem junto.** Você precisa do seu próprio dump de *Tears of the Kingdom* com a atualização **1.4.3** aplicada (`exefs` e `romfs`, ou o `romfs` como um único `romfs.bin`).

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **FSR 1 (EASU) na metade do tempo:**
  - A análise de borda roda uma vez por pixel, em vez de quatro.
  - Onde não há borda, o pixel sai direto da interpolação bilinear.
  - As contas de cor usam meia precisão, que vira fp16 onde o driver aceita.
  - No POCO F7 Ultra (Adreno 830), o upscale de 1280x717 para 1920x1080 caiu de 1,00 para 0,50 ms por quadro. Não vi diferença nas bordas lado a lado.
  - Ideias do artigo "Optimizing FSR", de atyuwen, reescritas a partir do FSR 1 original.
- **FXAA ~18% mais leve:**
  - Usa meia precisão e o limiar padrão do FXAA 3.11, em vez do "ultra".
  - A busca da borda é mais curta: 5 passos em vez de 10.
  - No POCO caiu de 0,51-0,59 para 0,43-0,44 ms por quadro, sem diferença de serrilhado visível.

releases.name: TOTKDroid 0.3.2 (beta): magenta com Economia de RAM e 2-3 fps na Mali corrigidos
releases.body:
**Beta 0.3.2.** Corrige dois problemas da 0.3.1: os **quadrados magenta com a Economia de RAM ligada** ([#57](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/57)) e a **queda para 2-3 fps no mundo aberto em algumas Mali** (Dimensity 9500, [#41](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/41)).

> **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem junto.** Você precisa do seu próprio dump de *Tears of the Kingdom* com a atualização **1.4.3** aplicada (`exefs` e `romfs`, ou o `romfs` como um único `romfs.bin`).

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **Quadrados magenta com a Economia de RAM ([#57](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/57)):**
  - A 0.3.1 devolvia ao sistema a memória de cada textura depois de enviá-la à GPU, o que deixava zeros no lugar. O TOTK reaproveita essa memória para criar texturas novas, que então eram enviadas zeradas e apareciam magenta.
  - Isso agora fica desligado. A Economia de RAM continua usando texturas menores e menos memória de cópia.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.5-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.5-dev (versionCode 9).

### Changes

- Added native implementations of selected game, rendering, AI and container algorithms, with the original recompiled paths retained. Optimized guest-register handling, x87 calculations and indirect-call caches.
- Added Optimal (ARM64) and Exact (x86) execution modes. Exact selects the original recompiled algorithms; both modes run as ARM64 code.
- Reduced GLES state traffic between threads, draw preparation work and shader constant uploads, and improved shader program caching.
- Improved launcher operation progress, diagnostics and Play button feedback, with the amber UT3 palette.
- Added an optional 4 GB guest address space, enabled by default on 64-bit devices with at least 5 GiB of RAM.
- Fixed fingerprint sensors being mistaken for gamepads.
- Reduced APK size by stripping non-runtime library symbols while retaining the original library for offline profiling. Expanded regression tests and updated documentation.

### Requirements

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.4.1-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4.1-dev (versionCode 8).

### Changes

- Improved CPU performance on PhysX Mod Pack maps with native fluid collision kernels, native pair removal and optimized x87 calculations.
- Added on-device HLSL compilation through vkd3d-shader, with shader caching and improved MojoShader compatibility for mod materials.
- Fixed touch aiming: holding Fire no longer blocks another finger's camera movement; dragging from Fire, secondary fire, Jump or Crouch also turns the camera.
- Made the crash monitor a launcher option, disabled by default, to avoid keeping its extra Android process running unless needed.
- Removed FSR3 frame generation. FSR1 spatial upscaling and FXAA remain available.
- Reduced per-draw post-processing overhead and removed temporary qa-flags performance switches.
- Updated localized PhysX and audio setting descriptions.

### Installation and validation

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; compatible Adreno devices can use Turnip.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.4-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4-dev.

### Changes

- Added an FPS counter with a frame-time graph and optional system information for every renderer.
- Added FSR1, FXAA, and FSR3.1 frame generation (DXVK, Android 12+; disabled by default).
- Added CPU-based PhysX effects and OpenAL Soft audio through AAudio with EAX 1–5 support.
- Added a maximum-graphics button and fixed persistence of the 3D rendering scale.
- Fixed terrain rendering in OpenGL ES, accelerated DXT decoding, and allowed unused texture mip levels to stream out.
- Improved GPU query handling in GLES and DXVK, including on PowerVR devices.
- Fixed ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion on shared storage on Pixel devices.
- Added a “Firing or aiming” gyroscope mode and persistent crash reports with a separate error window.

### Installation and limitations

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; frame generation requires Android 12+. Frame generation may cause HUD artifacts and adds GPU and memory overhead. A stable 60 FPS at maximum graphics settings is not guaranteed.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.3-dev
releases.body:
The third release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 improves GLES performance, text editing and graphics cache handling.

### Changes

- Added a dedicated GLES render thread with automatic CPU core selection. Streamed draw uploads, asynchronous query polling and shader program prelinking reduce work on the game thread.
- Added driver-aware graphics cache maintenance: GLES program binaries are invalidated after driver changes, and DXVK keeps the current and newest other pipeline cache for each driver.
- Fixed DXVK scaled vertex formats with a shader fallback for drivers that need it.
- Replaced keyboard-only text entry with an Android editing dialog for game fields, console commands and chat. Existing text can be corrected or cleared; cancellation preserves it, and original character filters remain in effect.
- Added separate weapon-button swipe settings and expanded the in-game Android settings to nine languages: English, Russian, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian and Polish.
- Improved launcher texture status and fixed texture handling, audio and FSINCOS translation. Expanded regression tests and rendering diagnostics.

### Requirements

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 0.2-dev
releases.body:
The second release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 adds optional texture conversion, more flexible touch controls, OpenSpy compatibility and save/profile fixes.

### Changes

- Added optional ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion in the launcher, including games played directly from stored ZIP archives. Original packages are retained; runtime DXT decoding remains available for cache misses and mods.
- Added a touch layout editor to move, resize and hide individual controls. Hold the on-screen Pause button to open it; a short tap opens the original pause menu.
- Expanded touch settings with a fixed joystick, weapon tap/swipe selection, separate weapon bar/wheel sizes, control visibility, movement while holding primary fire and horizontal gyro reversal.
- Added OpenSpy service and authentication compatibility, and fixed a registry-call crash during online play.
- Prevented startup defaults from overwriting saved profiles and campaign progress before sign-in. Fixed creation of save directories beneath virtual ZIP folders.

releases.name: v0.7.7
releases.body:
v0.7.7 fixes the Android surface orientation: the v0.7.6 build restored the identity-preferred swapchain preTransform that had shipped in v0.7.5, and on devices reporting ROTATE_90 the composer applied that rotation a second time to an already-upright window-space blit. The first release of Odin.

Odin (ᚨ) is a low-level emulator of the SEGA Hikaru arcade board. It runs the programs of the real chips wherever they are known, and draws with OpenGL or Vulkan. It is a hard fork of Valkyrie, by Stefano Teso.

All six Hikaru games, two of them in two versions:

- Air Trix (`airtrix`, `airtrixo`)
- Brave Firefighters (`braveff`)
- Planet Harriers (`pharrier`)
- NASCAR Arcade (`sgnascar`, `sgnascaro`)
- Star Wars Racer Arcade (`swracer`)
- Cyber Troopers Virtual-On Force (`von4`)

They play with a keyboard, mice, gamepads, wheels with force feedback (NASCAR) or light guns (Brave Firefighters). Each game is a MAME ROM and needs the BIOS `hikaru.zip` and `mie.zip` too.

直接下载下方 APK (约 325 MB) 安装即可, 无需额外组件。首次启动会自动解包 rootfs。

- **Um jogo não alcança mais os arquivos do computador.** Um `.mod` aberto fora de um pacote,
  direto de uma pasta como `Downloads`, podia mexer nos arquivos ao lado dele: ler, trocar o
  conteúdo e apagar. Num pacote `.zip`, podia apagar arquivos do próprio jogo. Nenhum jogo da
  biblioteca faz isso, mas um `.mod` de origem desconhecida faria. Agora:
  - o jogo só lê o que veio com ele, e não consegue alterar nem apagar esses arquivos;
  - tudo o que o jogo grava vai para a pasta de saves do emulador;
  - atalhos (links simbólicos) dentro da pasta do jogo são ignorados;
  - um save state alterado à mão não reabre arquivos fora do que o jogo alcança.
- **Os saves de todos os jogos ficam juntos**, em `saves/mod/`, uma pasta por jogo, como no
  console. Um jogo que usa o save de outro, como o Zeebo F.C. com os bonecos do Zeeboids,
  continua encontrando o que precisa

# v0.5.0

O Ultimate Chess 3D, o Alice no País das Maravilhas, o Rally Master Pro e o menu do Quake voltam a
funcionar, e a água do Bóia Cross ganha a cor do console. Carregar um save state e usar o rewind

de reiniciar o jogo, no Qt e no Android.

**A interface em Qt ganha cara nova e save states.** Temas, menus, barra de ferramentas e de
status, configurações com barra lateral, e o jogo abre na própria janela principal. Os save states
chegam ao Qt com dez slots por jogo e atalhos de teclado, e o Android passa de cinco para dez
slots.

**A interface antiga, em egui, saiu.** O emulador passa a ter uma interface só, a em Qt, que já
era a principal desde a v0.4.0 e é a que recebe as novidades.

Para quem usava a interface em egui (o programa `zeebx`, o pacote `zeebx-standalone-egui` ou o
cask `zeebxteam/tap/zeebx`):

- ela fica na v0.4.2 e **não vai receber atualizações**. O emulador não troca uma interface pela
  outra sozinho;
- para continuar recebendo as versões novas, instale a interface em Qt pela página de releases

**Experimental.** Tested on one phone only (vivo X300 Pro, Dimensity 9500, Mali-G1-Ultra MC12, vendor driver `v1.r54p1`). Expect rendering bugs, hangs and crashes.

## What's new since v0.3.4

- **Fixed: games added from a USB stick or SD card now see their whole folder.** Picking an exe deep inside a game folder (for example `<stick>/Cyberpunk 2077/bin/x64/Cyberpunk2077.exe`) used to make only `bin/x64` visible to the game, so `archive/`, `engine/` and `r6/` were missing. The app now makes the game's root folder visible (the first folder below the stick or card, or the game's own folder inside a container such as `Games/`). The stick's top folder itself is never bound. Internal storage is unchanged.
- **One-time repair of games added before this fix.** On the first start, games added from a stick or card with the old exe-folder binding are moved to their game root once. Their entries, start-in folders and launch options keep working, and their Steam shortcut ids stay the same. If the stick is unplugged at that moment, nothing is dropped: the repair waits and retries (at most once a minute) until the stick is back.

releases.body:
**Experimental.** Tested on one phone only (vivo X300 Pro, Dimensity 9500, Mali-G1-Ultra MC12, vendor driver `v1.r54p1`). Expect rendering bugs, hangs and crashes.

## What's new since v0.2.0

- **DX12 ray tracing (DXR) through an emulated ray-tracing pipeline.** The vendor driver has ray queries only. The compat layer now emulates `VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline` on top of them (each RT pipeline becomes one ray-query compute megakernel, the acceleration-structure calls are emulated), which is what vkd3d-proton's DXR needs. **Opt-in, off by default**, and heavy on GPU memory.
  - **How to turn it on:**
    1. In DroidDeck switch on **"Ray tracing: DX12 games (DXR)"** (Performance panel, or the game's own panel). It sets `BL_DXR=1`, which sets `MALI_COMPAT_RT_PIPELINE=1` for the game. You can also set `MALI_COMPAT_RT_PIPELINE=1` in the game's environment.
    2. The app does not set the vkd3d-proton keys yet. In the game's environment add `VKD3D_CONFIG=dxr,dxr11,no_upload_hvv,single_queue,extra_rtas_sync` (the app's default for The Witcher 3 is `nodxr`, so this key replaces it).
